transcript:
00:00 Alex (Redwood AE): okay everyone thanks for joining, um, shoot we'll run through the numbers and then priya will talk through the tuning notes.
00:27 Jordan (Borealis ML): cool, we're seeing the baseline numbers from IncumbentAI here, p50 is fine but p99 is all over the place, so curious what you have.
00:45 Priya (Redwood SE): yeah so quick context, we ran head-to-head with the same model family, lightweight quant, and a routing profile that prefers low-latency pool first then fallback. our p50 vs baseline is about 15ms lower, p99 is about 70ms lower in most windows.
01:12 Aaron (Borealis Infra): the curious bit for us is throughput — under burst we hit a throttle at 800 rps on your dedicated slot but incumbent seemed to degrade earlier? can you explain why we saw the spike?
01:38 Priya (Redwood SE): right, so two things — our runtime does continuous batching and will hold a microbatch for up to 8ms to coalesce tokens, that increases throughput efficiency for mid-size payloads. the incumbent uses a fixed micro-batch that doesn't adapt, so under burst they drop into head-of-line blocking.
02:05 Maya (Borealis PM): is that batching tunable by us? like if our app needs lower latency at lower throughput can we shift knobs?
02:22 Priya (Redwood SE): absolutely, you can set the latency SLO target and the autoscaler will change the batch window / slot allocation. we'll share a tuning doc.
02:50 Jordan (Borealis ML): I did notice an odd KV cache miss pattern — some warm prefixes still looked cold on repeat queries. could be our prompt prep or the runtime?
03:12 Priya (Redwood SE): we saw that in the logs — in one run the K V cache key normalization had a casing mismatch, transcription note, like 'K V cash' in old logs, so we added a normalization layer. it's likely whitespace/zero-width char in your prompt pipeline.
03:45 Aaron (Borealis Infra): ok that explains some variability. on security, Talia do you need anything else from Redwood to accept Private?
04:03 Talia (Borealis InfoSec): we need KMS integration flow, key rotation policy, and audit-log retention options. also SOC2 type II evidence and paper trail for SSO.
04:25 Samir (Redwood CSM): we'll send the security pack; Alex will drive the KMS example for your HSM workflow.
04:40 Alex (Redwood AE): quick demo of the dashboard numbers — Samir can you pull the send rate vs success rate chart?
05:02 Samir (Redwood CSM): yep, sharing my screen... (pause) ok, here's the chart. you can see at minute 18 of the run the incumbent had a spike in errors while Redwood maintained throughput but with a small latency bump.
05:28 Jordan (Borealis ML): do you have raw logs? we want to compare token-emit traces to see where stalls happen.
05:40 Priya (Redwood SE): yes we will upload the raw traces to the shared bucket; note the traces include per-token kernel selection timestamps — sometimes the selection path for longer contexts picks a fallback kernel which adds ~20ms.
06:03 Maya (Borealis PM): what's the recommended path for us: keep hosted API for now or move to Dedicated? we're worried about predictability.
06:20 Alex (Redwood AE): for this POC, Dedicated is good because you get predictable throughput; we can later show how Redwood Private/ VPC maps if you need on-prem controls.
06:48 Jordan (Borealis ML): one more thing — cost. the incumbent gave us a lower per-token sticker but with hidden prefetch charges. can you run a cost comparison including quantization and routing hit rates?
07:05 Priya (Redwood SE): yes — we'll run two cost sims: one that favors extreme quant (int4) and one that keeps fp16 for quality. also we'll include cache hit improvements.
07:30 Maya (Borealis PM): timeline — if we want to decide by end of month, what's the gating criteria?
07:45 Alex (Redwood AE): p99 latency below 120ms for short queries, throughput sustaining 1k rps for 10 minutes without error rate increase >0.5%, and security signoff.
08:12 Jordan (Borealis ML): ok that's helpful. let's talk about the stress test you offered.
08:25 Priya (Redwood SE): plan: we'll provision an extra dedicated slot and run a 10k-message load test with traffic shapes you gave; we'll also flip routing thresholds to force fallback to cheaper model to measure quality deltas.
08:50 Aaron (Borealis Infra): please flag if the test needs IP allowlists changed for our VPC.
09:05 Priya (Redwood SE): noted — we'll provide exact IPs and temporary certs.
09:18 Talia (Borealis InfoSec): for KMS, we need to see a sample CSR for HSM and details on key import.
09:32 Alex (Redwood AE): we'll send a KMS walkthrough and sample CSR. Samir will attach SOC2 docs.
09:48 Jordan (Borealis ML): on the routing anomalies, do you have an explanation for the one minute regressions at the 22m mark?
10:02 Priya (Redwood SE): that was a scheduler preemption event — the cluster scaled down due to a probe and one worker got reclaimed then later warmed back, the fallback route kicked in and added ~55ms. we tuned the probe settings after that iteration.
10:28 Jordan (Borealis ML): great. does the console surface that event-level trace?
10:40 Samir (Redwood CSM): yes, you can click into the request and see per-worker kernel timing and routing decisions.
11:05 Maya (Borealis PM): action items recap?
11:18 Alex (Redwood AE): Alex will run 3-run routing experiment and post logs, Priya will validate cache normalization and do the long-context run, Samir send SOC2 and console walkthrough, Maya to update success-criteria doc, Talia to confirm KMS acceptance.
11:45 Jordan (Borealis ML): sounds good. any blockers?
11:52 Talia (Borealis InfoSec): only timeline for legal signoff, might take two weeks, but KMS answers will help.
12:05 Alex (Redwood AE): ok we'll push the stress test mid next week and aim to share cost sims before your next sync. thanks all.
12:20 (meeting ends)
